result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.minimum_cycle_basis()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a minimum weight cycle basis for the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L9800-L9884){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.minimum_cycle_basis(weight=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A minimum cycle basis is a cycle basis where the sum of weights of all cycles is minimized. For unweighted graphs, this minimizes the sum of cycle lengths. This implements a variant of Horton's algorithm: 1. for each edge `(u,v)`, find the shortest path from `u` to `v` not using `(u,v)` 2. this gives a candidate cycle for each edge 3. sort candidates by weight and greedily select linearly independent cycles ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge attribute name to use as weight. If `None`, uses the default edge weight (or `1.0` if edges don't have weights). The algorithm finds the basis that minimizes the sum of cycle weights. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of cycles forming a minimum weight cycle basis. Each cycle is a list of node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on a directed graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: O(E * V^2) for Horton's algorithm variant. - the minimum cycle basis is unique in terms of total weight (though there may be multiple bases with the same minimum weight). - works on disconnected graphs (finds minimum basis for each component). - for simple (unweighted) cycle basis, use `cycle_basis()` which is faster. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find minimum cycle basis of an unweighted graph: ::: {#200b578b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Two triangles sharing an edge graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") .add_edge("B", "D") .add_edge("D", "C") ) basis = graph.minimum_cycle_basis() # Returns 2 (the two triangles, sum of cycle lengths is minimized: 3 + 3 = 6) len(basis) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Find minimum cycle basis with edge weights: ::: {#fb9e793a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B", weight=1.0) .add_edge("B", "C", weight=2.0) .add_edge("C", "A", weight=3.0) ) basis = graph.minimum_cycle_basis(weight="weight") # Returns the triangle with total weight 6.0 ``` :::
